description:
Mandatory data: Battery chemistry; critical raw materials; materials used in the cathode, anode, and 
electrolyte; hazardous substances; impact of substances on the environment and on human health or 
safety.

Text.description: Describes a Property which contains plain text. This is intended exclusively for human readable strings, not for identifiers, measurement values, etc.

BatteryChemistryEntityList.description:
Detailed composition, including materials used in the cathode, anode, and electrolyte.
All common cells have two electrodes and an electrolyte. The specific combination of materials used to make these components is called "chemistry." A cell's chemistry largely determines its properties, while most variations within it are caused by additives, purification, and design elements.

EUBR: Annex XIII (1b) ? Annex VI Part A (7)

BatteryMaterialLocation.description: Battery component that relates to the material.

BatteryMaterialIdentifier.description:
Identifier of material. 

   The materials should be named using a public standard or agreed nomenclature, 
   which refers e.g. to the nomenclature of IUPAC or related identifiers such as the CAS (Chemical Abstracts Service) number. 
   
   
DIN DKE Spec 99100:2025-02 chapter reference: 6.5.4 k)

BatteryMaterialName.description:
Clear name of Material.

 Alphanumeric character string which describes the object.

BatteryMaterialMass.description: Weight of component material in Kilogram.

IsCriticalRawMaterial.description:
The battery passport must contain information on the critical raw materials present in the battery.

The information on the critical raw materials must also be provided on the battery label.
Per Annex VI, Part A(10), critical raw materials must be reported if present in the battery in a concentration of more than 0,1 % weight by weight.

BatteryMaterialList.description:
Detailed composition, including materials used in the cathode, anode, and electrolyte

EUBR: Annex XIII (2a)

HazardousSubstanceLocation.description: Location on a (sub-)component-level of a hazardous substance.

HazardousSubstance.description: Hazardous substances (No. 19-23): Name (agreed substance nomenclature, e.g. IUPAC or chemical name) all hazardous substance (as any substance that poses a threat to human health and the environment'). Suggested above 0.1 % weight by weight within each (sub-)component.

HazardousSubstanceClass.description: Battery Regulation narrows reporting to substances falling under defined hazard classes and categories of the CLP regulation.

HazardousSubstanceImpact.description: Impact statements based on, e.g., REACH or GHS for all hazard classes applicable to substances in the battery.

HazardousSubstanceLocation.description: Location on a (sub-)component-level of the hazardous substance

HazardousSubstancesList.description:
Hazardous substances contained in the battery other than mercury, cadmium or lead. Substance as a chemical element and its compounds in the natural state or the result of a manufacturing process (ECHA). Battery Regulation narrows reporting to substances falling under defined hazard classes and categories of the CLP regulation.

EUBR: Annex XIII (1b) ? Annex VI Part A (8)

BatteryChemistry.description:
Composition of a product in general terms by specifying the cathode and anode active material as well as electrolyte.
	
	
DIN DKE Spec 99100:2025-02 chapter reference: 6.5.2

BatteryMaterials.description:
Information on the detailed composition of the battery.
	
	Information on the detailed composition must include materials used in the cathode, anode and electrolyte.
	
	Materials in the battery should be reported above a concentration of 1% weight by weight. Thereby, the threshold of 1% should be determined as the overall content of the material in the battery in relation to the mass of the entire battery.
	Critical raw materials must be reported if present in the battery in a concentration of more than 0,1% weight by weight.
	
	
DIN DKE Spec 99100:2025-02 chapter reference: 6.5.3-6.5.4

HazardousSubstances.description:
Information on hazardous substances other than mercury, cadmium, or lead contained in the battery.
	
    Hazardous substances also being substances of very high concern, as defined under the RegulationEC No1907/2006 (“REACH Regulation”) should be reported on if exceeding a threshold of 0,1% weight by weight.
	
	
DIN DKE Spec 99100:2025-02 chapter reference: 6.5.4 - 6.5.6
